summary_hint: TRID Loan Estimate for <borrower_name> on loan <loan_number>: amount <loan_amount> at <interest_rate>, APR <apr>, rate lock to <rate_lock_expiration>, cash to close <cash_to_close>.

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — the loan id (Loan ID #); the join key to the file's other documents
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Loan ID #', captured verbatim; masked + hashed at the snapshot boundary

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — the applicant/borrower; match to the file

typed_core.name: sale_price
typed_core.why: processor — 'Sale Price' (or 'Est. Prop. Value' on a refinance)

typed_core.name: interest_rate
typed_core.why: processor — 'Interest Rate' (the initial rate if it can increase)
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Interest Rate' — the initial rate as printed

typed_core.name: loan_product
typed_core.why: processor — the product (e.g. 'Fixed Rate', an ARM product)

typed_core.name: lender_name
typed_core.prompt_hint: the lender named at the top of the form

typed_core.name: apr
typed_core.why: processor — Annual Percentage Rate (page-3 Comparisons); a number a processor checks
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Annual Percentage Rate (APR)' in the Comparisons box (page 3)

typed_core.name: estimated_total_monthly_payment
typed_core.why: processor — 'Estimated Total Monthly Payment' (the FIRST-period value if it varies)
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Estimated Total Monthly Payment' — the first period's value if the schedule steps

typed_core.name: prepayment_penalty_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — whether the loan has a prepayment penalty (YES/NO)

typed_core.name: balloon_payment_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — whether the loan has a balloon payment (YES/NO)

typed_core.name: rate_lock_expiration
typed_core.why: processor — the rate-lock expiration (LE-only). NOTE: CL-1 reads a rate-LOCK CONFIRMATION, not the LE; this is the LE's own printed lock expiry, captured as a fact
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'RATE LOCK ... until <date> at <time>' — capture the expiration date

typed_core.name: closing_cost_estimate_expiration
typed_core.why: processor — when the estimated closing costs expire (LE-only)
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'All other estimated closing costs expire on <date>'

typed_core.name: in_5_years_total_payments
typed_core.why: processor — the 'In 5 Years' total paid (principal, interest, MI, loan costs) — the LE Comparisons box (LE-only)

typed_core.name: in_5_years_principal_paid
typed_core.why: processor — the 'In 5 Years' principal paid off (LE-only)

rejected.name: finance_charge / amount_financed / total_of_payments
rejected.reason: ⚠️ CD-ONLY. The LE has NO 'Loan Calculations' box — its page-3 'Comparisons' gives In-5-Years + APR + TIP instead. Including these on the LE would create three permanently-null fields on every LE (the LP-461 lesson, applied before building). They live on closing_disclosure only.

rejected.name: closing_date / disbursement_date / seller_name / settlement_agent
rejected.reason: CD-only — an LE is issued early, has no closing/disbursement date, no seller, no settlement agent.

rejected.name: A-J itemized cost tables / transaction summaries / AIR table
rejected.reason: serve out-of-scope TRID/ARM rules; the headline totals are captured; Tier 3 carries the rest (ADR).

rejected.name: contact information block (page 3)
rejected.reason: lender/broker contact names, NMLS IDs, phones — not captured (avoids phone/NMLS PII for a visibility type); Tier 3.

encoding_variations: the LE is the standard ~3-page TRID form; the headline spans page 1 (Loan Terms / Projected Payments / Costs at Closing) + page 3 (Comparisons: In 5 Years, APR, TIP)
the LE has NO seller column and NO disbursement date (both CD-only) — a strong CD-vs-LE separator
sale_price is 'Sale Price' (purchase) or 'Est. Prop. Value' (refinance)
RATE LOCK prints 'until <date> at <time>' and 'estimated closing costs expire on <date>' — the two LE expirations
on an ARM the rate can increase ('YES', 'goes as high as ...', AIR table page 2); interest_rate is the initial rate

open_questions.q: Headline block vs the full LE?
open_questions.recommendation: HEADLINE ONLY (GEET'S DECISION, LP-470): no in-scope rule reads an LE; Tier 1 on processor visibility. Tier 3 carries the itemization.

notes: loan_estimate was an existing Tier-2 catalog type; this PROMOTES it to Tier 1 with the headline schema (~80% shared with closing_disclosure). LE-only: rate_lock_expiration, closing_cost_estimate_expiration, in_5_years_total_payments, in_5_years_principal_paid.
No in-scope rule reads it — Tier 1 on processor visibility (wire_instructions / ACORD 25 standard).
PII: only loan_number (reuses the global registration). No account numbers in the headline; the contact block is not captured.
